findings.old_behavior: SAX characters() and cdataBlock() callbacks in xmlParseReference receive the xmlParserCtxt pointer (ctxt) as their first context argument. This is inconsistent with other SAX callbacks in the same function (e.g. reference() at line 7245) and with documented SAX semantics where the first argument should be ctxt->userData.
findings.new_behavior: SAX characters() and cdataBlock() callbacks now receive ctxt->userData as their first context argument, consistent with the documented SAX API and with other callbacks in xmlParseReference.
findings.compatibility_reason: SAX users who register custom characters() or cdataBlock() callbacks and set userData explicitly (via xmlNewSAXParserCtxt or by setting ctxt->userData) will receive their userData pointer instead of the parser context. Previously the callback incorrectly received the xmlParserCtxt* value, which could cause crashes, wrong behavior, or silent data corruption if the callback casts ctx to a non-xmlParserCtxt type, or misdirected behavior if the callback relied on receiving the parser context directly. Users who leave userData as the default (which equals ctxt) will see no change.
findings.why_not_internal_only: SAX callbacks are a public API surface of libxml2. The xmlSAXHandler struct is defined in public headers (SAX.h, SAX2.h), and the characters/cdataBlock callbacks are invoked for all SAX-based parsing users. Changing the context pointer passed to these callbacks affects any consumer using SAX parsing with custom userData.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. The change is deterministic and its effect is clear. The only ambiguity is whether existing SAX consumers always rely on receiving ctxt vs userData, which depends on individual usage patterns.
findings.recommended_review: Review SAX-based parsers in dependent projects to check if characters/cdataBlock callbacks cast the ctx parameter to xmlParserCtxt* or expect it to be the parser context. Projects using the default userData setting (ctxt->userData == ctxt) are unaffected.
findings.test_recommendation: PCAT-P019: Write a small SAX handler that records the ctx pointer received in characters() and cdataBlock() callbacks during entity reference parsing, and assert that the pointer equals the userData passed to xmlNewSAXParserCtxt (not the parser context). Generic parser success alone is insufficient; the callback data pointer identity must be verified explicitly.
